# AGENTS.md — Autonomous Agent Onboarding

## Project Overview

Full-stack monorepo for long-running manufacturing workflows (Build, Parts, TestRun) with type-safe end-to-end automation.

**Stack:** Angular 19+ | Hot Chocolate GraphQL | ASP.NET Core (.NET 10) | Elsa Workflows v3 | SQL Server 2022 | EF Core + Dapper

**Key Property:** Type-safe pipeline: C# entities → `schema.graphql` (auto-emitted on `dotnet build`) → `graphql.ts` (auto-generated via `pnpm codegen`)

---

## Setup & Verification Commands

**Prerequisites:** Docker Desktop, .NET SDK 10+, Node.js 18+, pnpm 8+

```bash
# Dependencies
pnpm install                    # Frontend + monorepo
dotnet restore                  # Backend packages

# Infrastructure
pnpm docker:up                  # Start SQL Server (port 1433)
pnpm db:migrate                 # Apply EF Core migrations

# Build
pnpm build                      # Full build (backend + frontend)
pnpm build:backend              # dotnet build
pnpm build:frontend             # Angular build

# Test (requires Docker)
pnpm test                       # Full suite
pnpm test:backend               # dotnet test
pnpm test:frontend              # Vitest + Testing Library

# Code Generation & Quality
pnpm codegen                    # Regenerate graphql.ts from schema.graphql
pnpm lint                       # Frontend linting

# Cleanup
pnpm docker:down                # Stop SQL Server
pnpm docker:clean               # Remove volumes
```

---

## Coding & Style Guidelines

### Frontend (Angular)

- **Mandatory `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`** on all components (avoid dirty-check cycles)
- **Required `trackBy` function** on every `*ngFor` loop (performance critical; see [[frontend-patterns]])
- **Never manually edit `graphql.ts`** — auto-generated by `pnpm codegen`; regenerate after backend schema changes
- **Use generated types only** — import from `src/app/api/generated/graphql.ts`; never hand-roll type aliases

### Backend (ASP.NET Core + EF Core + Dapper)

- **EF Core + Dapper in same operation must share explicit `DbTransaction`** — forgetting causes factory-floor deadlocks (see [[database-rules]])
- **Never return raw EF Core entities** — map to DTOs via `.ProjectTo<DTO>()`
- **DataLoaders required** for child-entity queries (Build → Parts → TestRuns); add `[UseProjection]` to resolvers
- **GraphQL query depth: maximum 5 layers** — split deeper queries into separate requests (see [[graphql-patterns]])

### Workflows (Elsa v3)

- **Store only primitives** (Guid, string) in workflow variables — never store complex objects
- Fetch fresh domain state on activity execution (objects become stale quickly in long-running workflows)
- Treat activities as stateless handlers; pass IDs, not entity graphs

---

## Agent Guardrails & Boundaries

### ❌ NEVER

- ❌ Manually edit `frontend/src/app/api/generated/graphql.ts` (auto-generated; run `pnpm codegen`)
- ❌ Manually edit `backend/src/FactoryApp.WebApi/schema.graphql` (auto-emitted on `dotnet build`; commit to repo)
- ❌ Create EF Core + Dapper writes without explicit shared `DbTransaction` — deadlock risk
- ❌ Return raw EF Core entities in GraphQL resolvers — use DTOs (see [[graphql-patterns]])
- ❌ Create `*ngFor` loops without `trackBy` functions — performance killer
- ❌ Mock `DbContext` in tests — use real SQL Server (connection: `Server=localhost,1433;Database=FactoryAppDb_Test;...`)
- ❌ Create GraphQL queries > 5 layers deep — split into separate requests
- ❌ Store complex objects in Elsa workflow variables — use primitives only (Guid, string)
- ❌ Implement Issue #147 (rate limiting) before Issue #148 (authorization) is complete
- ❌ Implement Issue #149 (workflows) before Issue #148 (authorization) is merged

### ✅ DO

- ✅ Run `dotnet build` → `pnpm codegen` after any schema changes (type-safety pipeline)
- ✅ Run full test suite (`pnpm test`) after architecture changes
- ✅ Use TypeScript/C# strict mode; never suppress type errors
- ✅ Add `trackBy` to every `*ngFor` loop — function signature: `(index: number, item: T) => any`
- ✅ Share `DbTransaction` for composite mutations: `using var txn = await context.Database.BeginTransactionAsync()`
- ✅ Use `[UseProjection]` on GraphQL resolvers to optimize SELECT columns
- ✅ Follow exact issue order: **Issue #148 (authorization) → #149 (workflows) → #147 (rate limiting)**

### ⚠️ SPECIAL RULES

- **Type-Safety Pipeline**: Code generation is part of the build. If C# schema changes → `dotnet build` updates `schema.graphql` → `pnpm codegen` updates `graphql.ts`. Front-end and back-end must regenerate and test together.
- **Mutations with Multiple Operations**: EF Core + Dapper writes in same operation must wrap in explicit `DbTransaction`; forgetting causes deadlocks on factory floor.
- **Elsa Workflow Versioning**: Always version new workflows; never force-update active runs. Allow old versions to complete naturally.
- **Query Complexity**: Limit GraphQL query depth to 5 layers. Use DataLoaders + separate requests for deeper hierarchies.
